record.paper_title: Revisiting the foundations of the quantum theory of atoms in molecules: Some open problems
record.original_question: How can one define an origin-independent energy for a topological atom when the molecular Hamiltonian contains non-Coulombic, inhomogeneous, or marginally modified potential-energy terms? The desired definition must work when the usual Coulombic homogeneity used in the subsystem virial theorem fails, including potentials that are sums of homogeneous terms of different degrees or are not finitely decomposable into homogeneous terms.

evidence.quote: 2.2. How to extend the concept of topological atom’s “energy” for non-coulombic interactions?

Any marginal modification of the coulombic potential energy in a molecular system, e.g. using any of the finite nucleus models instead of the point charge model [76] or adding terms corresponding to various small magnetic interactions [77,78], destroys the homogeneity of the potential energy function, making the originally proposed procedure useless.

The local version of the subsystem virial theorem is now: and evidently, this equation cannot be used to propose a proper form for to guarantee the origin independence of the topological atom’s energy.

However, this procedure is too crude to be seen as a proper solution and we leave the proper definition of topological atom’s energy upon marginal modification of the coulombic potential as an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. In the quantum theory of atoms in molecules, a "topological atom" Ω is a basin in three-dimensional space bounded by a zero-flux surface of the gradient field of the electron density ρ(r) of a stationary molecular state, i.e. ∇ρ(r)·n(r)=0 for all r on the boundary ∂Ω, where n(r) is the outward unit normal. For a molecular Hamiltonian whose potential energy V is a homogeneous function of degree k in the nuclear–electronic coordinates (e.g. the purely Coulombic case, k=−1), the subsystem (regional) virial theorem provides an origin-independent definition of the energy E(Ω) of the topological atom, by combining the kinetic energy density integrated over Ω with a virial contribution whose origin dependence is canceled using the homogeneity (Euler) relation r·∇V = kV.

Problem. Provide a general, mathematically well-defined prescription for the energy E(Ω) of a topological atom that is independent of the choice of coordinate origin in the laboratory frame, in each of the following situations where the standard homogeneity argument fails:

(a) V is a finite sum V = Σ_i V_i where each V_i is homogeneous of a different degree k_i (for example, Coulombic terms supplemented by finite-nucleus charge-distribution potentials, or by magnetic interaction terms breaking translation–scaling homogeneity).

(b) V cannot be written as a finite sum of homogeneous functions (i.e. it admits no finite homogeneous decomposition).

The prescription must (i) reduce to the usual Bader/QTAIM atomic energy when V is purely Coulombic, (ii) yield a value E(Ω) invariant under arbitrary translations of the spatial origin, (iii) satisfy an additivity property Σ_Ω E(Ω) = E_total over a partition of space into topological atoms, and (iv) be derivable from a local form of the subsystem virial theorem (or an appropriate generalization thereof) compatible with the non-homogeneous V.
artifact.category_tag: Quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM)
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface extensions of the QTAIM basin-energy procedure to non-Coulombic but homogeneous potentials (the QTROS framework), but no published prescription appears to handle inhomogeneous potentials such as finite-nucleus models or magnetic-interaction corrections in an origin-independent way. The problem of defining an origin-independent topological-atom energy beyond the homogeneous case appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Extending the Topological Analysis and Seeking the Real-Space Subsystems in Non-Coulombic Systems with Homogeneous Potential Energy Functions
status_evidence.snippet: For the subset of homogeneous potential energy functions, the regional virial theorem may be used to derive well-defined, origin-independent, basin energies.
status_evidence.claim: Existing extensions cover homogeneous (but non-Coulombic) potentials only, not the inhomogeneous case posed in the problem.

status_evidence.title: What is an Atom in a Molecule
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of QTAIM/QTROS basin energies and the role of homogeneity in the subsystem virial theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that origin-independence of basin energies relies on homogeneity of V, leaving the inhomogeneous case unresolved.
